name: RECOIL-v2
mechanism: Second OS persistence vector — winreg Run-key: a marker-tagged HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entry (stdlib winreg) carrying the engagement lab-UUID, created as a redundant persistence path alongside the scheduled task, both marker-gated and both covered by the same SHA-256 wipe.
what_it_does_previous_couldnt: R10/R11 gave a single persistence vector (schtasks). A defender who only hunts scheduled tasks would miss the Run-key survivor; two marker-tagged vectors make persistence genuinely redundant so the operator practices clearing BOTH registry and scheduler footpaths.
fireback: The operator clears the scheduled task but the Run-key still fires at next interactive logon; they must clear BOTH. Fireback = redundancy forces complete, not partial, cleanup practice — and the evidence journal shows both vectors so nothing is hidden by the tool.
containment: Run-key added only under HKCU (the operator's own hive), operator-consented with --confirm-lab, marker-tagged with the engagement uuid, value pointing only at a bundled loopback beacon; winreg is stdlib. The allowlist resolver re-validates the beacon host before it ever runs.
kill_switch: Wipe deletes the markered Run-value, re-reads the hive to assert its absence, and includes it in the SHA-256 zero-survivor audit alongside the scheduled-task clean; a --no-registry flag disables this vector entirely.
novelty_angle: Redundant, marker-gated, operator-owned persistence across two real win32 footpaths (scheduler + registry) both bounded by one provable kill-switch — turning single-path persistence into a redundancy-bounded recovery drill the operator must fully clear.
